Content: (a) SaaS question framing ('one row per (user, tag)'); (b) Keyword anchor surfacing 'UNNEST array column / explode array Trino / array to rows / one row per element / one row per tag / flatten array / LEFT JOIN UNNEST / CROSS JOIN UNNEST / keep empty array rows / preserve NULL array rows'; (c) two SQL forms side-by-side — FORM 1 CROSS JOIN UNNEST(u.tags) AS t(tag) with comment 'DROPS parent rows whose array is NULL or empty — semantically an INNER join', FORM 2 LEFT JOIN UNNEST(u.tags) AS t(tag) ON TRUE with comment 'KEEPS parent rows whose array is NULL or empty, emitting NULL in the unnested column. ON TRUE is the only join condition the LEFT JOIN UNNEST form supports.'; (d) rule-of-thumb (drop-NULLs-wrong → FORM 2, drop-NULLs-correct → FORM 1); (e) Trino docs cite to trino.io/docs/current/sql/select.html with the exact LEFT-JOIN-preferable quote; (f) one-sentence cross-ref note that the existing UNNEST(sequence(...)) patterns in §4 and §5 Pattern B2 never drop rows because sequence() never returns NULL/empty — preserves locked canonical §5 Pattern B2 by clarifying it doesn't need the preserve-rows fix. Used Section 1a (not §2-renumber) so downstream section numbers and the locked r07 §5 Pattern B2 are untouched. Total addition: ~28 lines including code block, well under 'tight 2-4 lines' if you count just the rule (the worked example takes the rest, which is necessary because FORM 1 vs FORM 2 contrast is the whole point). WEBSEARCH VERIFICATION (2 confirmations): (1) trino.io/docs/current/sql/select.html UNNEST section confirmed: 'LEFT JOIN is preferable in order to avoid losing the row containing the array/map field in question when referenced columns from relations on the left side of the join can be empty or have NULL values' AND 'When using LEFT JOIN, the only condition supported by the current implementation is ON TRUE.' (2) Worked example from docs confirms semantics — for input rows ('Joe', ARRAY[10,20,30,42]), ('Roger', ARRAY[10]), ('Dave', ARRAY[]), ('Levi', NULL): LEFT JOIN UNNEST ON TRUE returns 7 rows (Joe x4, Roger x1, Dave NULL, Levi NULL); CROSS JOIN UNNEST would return only 5 (Dave and Levi dropped). Both SQL forms are valid Trino 467 dialect (no QUALIFY, no concat_ws, no Postgres-isms; UNNEST + ARRAY(VARCHAR) + LEFT JOIN UNNEST ON TRUE all native Trino grammar per trino.io/docs/current/sql/select.html).
